title: Multi-Scale Self-Contrastive Learning with Hard Negative Mining for Weakly-Supervised Query-based Video Grounding

problems.name: Annotation Scarcity and Noisy Supervision
problems.evidence_sentence: Firstly, since we only resort to video-level annotations with no access to the frame-level knowledge, we propose frame-wise matching score prediction to estimate the score of each frame matched to the video-level annotations in a weakly-supervised manner, as well as the frame-wise matching weight via an attention mechanism in order to choose possible foreground frames with query semantics.

problems.name: Boundary Ambiguity and Localization Precision
problems.evidence_sentence: Secondly, since some predicted frames (i.e., boundary frames) are relatively coarse and exhibit similar appearance to their adjacent frames, we propose a coarse-to-fine contrastive learning paradigm to learn more discriminative frame-wise representations for distinguishing the false positive frames.

problems.name: Cross-Modal Semantic Alignment Gap
problems.evidence_sentence: Speciﬁcally, given the input video and query, we ﬁrst encode both visual and textual features, and align their semantics by a video-query attention mechanism to learn the cross-modal interactions.

methods.name: Coarse-to-Fine or Hierarchical Localization
methods.evidence_sentence: Multi-Scale Self-Contrastive Learning with Hard Negative Mining for Weakly-Supervised Query-based Video Grounding Query-based video grounding is an important yet challenging task in video understanding, which aims to localize the target segment in an untrimmed video according to a sentence query.

methods.name: Weak-Supervision and Pseudo-Label Correction
methods.evidence_sentence: Multi-Scale Self-Contrastive Learning with Hard Negative Mining for Weakly-Supervised Query-based Video Grounding Query-based video grounding is an important yet challenging task in video understanding, which aims to localize the target segment in an untrimmed video according to a sentence query.

methods.name: Contrastive or Cross-Modal Alignment
methods.evidence_sentence: Speciﬁcally, given the input video and query, we ﬁrst encode both visual and textual features, and align their semantics by a video-query attention mechanism to learn the cross-modal interactions.

methods.name: Transformer/DETR-Style Proposal Decoding
methods.evidence_sentence: In particular, instead of relying on redundant segment proposals for matching and selection, we propose to learn more ﬁnegrained frame-wise matching scores to predict whether each frame is the foreground frame.
